SubTopics: Model chromosome progression through meiosis and fertilization in order to argue how the processes of sexual reproduction lead to both genetic similarities and variation in diploid organisms. Compare and contrast the processes of sexual and asexual reproduction, identifying the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Content: The figure shows an event involving chromosomes that occurs during meiosis.
problems/TN25HSB/media/1a.jpg
How does this event affect the genetic variation of a population?

A.Choice: It reduces genetic variation in a population by creating new chromosomes that contain less DNA.

B.Choice: It reduces genetic variation in a population by creating genetically identical daughter cells from a parent cell.

C.Choice: It increases genetic variation in a population by creating DNA mutations that can be passed on to offspring.

D.Choice: It increases genetic variation in a population by creating gametes that contain new combinations of alleles.

SubTopics: Evaluate scientific data collected from analysis of molecular sequences, fossil records, biogeography, and embryology. Identify chronological patterns of change and communicate that biological evolution is supported by multiple lines of empirical evidence that identify similarities inherited from a common ancestor (homologies).
Content: Synapsids are a group of animals with a connected upper and lower jaw that allows movement of the jaw.

:ibox:• The earliest synapsids had `text(two)` bones called the quadrate (Q) and the articular (A) that made this connection.

• The most recent synapsids have `text(two)` different bones, the dentary (D) and the squamosal (S), that make this connection.
The figure shows changes in the jaw bones of synapsids over time.
problems/TN25HSB/media/2a.jpg
problems/TN25HSB/media/2b.jpg
Which `ultext(two)` statements about changes in synapsids over time are `ultext(best)` supported by the information in the figure?

A.Choice: The quadrate and articular bones disappeared before the dentary and squamosal bones appeared.

B.Choice: Species `text(Y)` is more closely related to Species `text(X)` than to Species `text(W)`.

C.Choice: The dentary and squamosal bones were present in the common ancestor for all `text(four)` species.

D.Choice: The common ancestor of Species `text(Y)` and Species `text(W)` had both the quadrate-articular and dentary-squamosal connections in all locations.

E.Choice: Species `text(X)` is a common ancestor of the other `text(three)` species.

problems/TN25HSB/media/3a.jpg
Which claim is `ultext(best)` supported using the data shown in the graph?

A.Choice: Between `1978-1995` the birth rate was equal to the death rate.

C.Choice: Around `1980` a contagious pathogen was introduced into the population.

Content: The reproductive cycle of the species Apis mellifera is known for producing offspring that have many gene sequences not found in the parent cells. Based on this information, a student claims that A. mellifera `ultext(most likely)` reproduces sexually rather than asexually.
Which `ultext(two)` pieces of evidence would `ultext(best)` support the student's claim?

A.Choice: A. mellifera combines chromosomes from `text(two)` gametes whenever it reproduces.

B.Choice: The body cells of A. mellifera have the same number of chromosomes as their gametes.

C.Choice: Homologous chromosomes in A. mellifera exchange genetic information within body cells.

D.Choice: A. mellifera produces specialized sex cells that contain the same genetic information as the parent cells.

E.Choice: Homologous chromosomes in A. mellifera exchange genetic information during the production of specialized sex cells.

SubTopics: Through pedigree analysis, identify patterns of trait inheritance to predict family member genotypes. Use mathematical thinking to predict the likelihood of various types of trait transmission.
Content: The time of `text(year)` during which a rose plant blooms, or flowers, is a trait called blooming seasonality. The blooming seasonality trait is controlled by the RoKSN gene. The RoKSN gene is a repressor gene that, when expressed, prohibits rose plants from blooming. The data table shows the blooming time associated with `text(two)` alleles of the RoKSN gene.
problems/TN25HSB/media/5a.jpg
How do differences between the RoKSN alleles `ultext(most likely)` account for the differences in the blooming seasonality trait in the `text(two)` types of roses?

A.Choice: Type `1` roses have an allele of the RoKSN gene that is expressed, so the rose plant blooms continuously.

B.Choice: Type `1` roses have an allele of the RoKSN gene that is not expressed, so the rose plant blooms continuously.

C.Choice: Type `2` roses have an allele of the RoKSN gene that is expressed, so the rose plant blooms continuously.

D.Choice: Type `2` roses have an allele of the RoKSN gene that is not expressed, so the rose plant blooms continuously.

Content: CYP3A5 is a protein that is important in metabolizing drugs in the liver. A student claims that some multipotent stem cells contain the gene for CYP3A5 production but others do not.
Based on the information in Figure `1` and Table `1` (Part `1`), is the claim supported?

A.Choice: Yes. All multipotent stem cells have the gene for CYP3A5 production, but it is only active in differentiated Cell type `text(W)`.

B.Choice: Yes. Only multipotent stem cells that differentiate into Cell type `text(Y)` have the gene for CYP3A5 production.

C.Choice: No. All multipotent stem cells have the gene for CYP3A5 production, but it is only active in differentiated Cell type `text(W)`.

D.Choice: No. Only multipotent stem cells that differentiate into Cell type `text(Y)` have the gene for CYP3A5 production.

Content: Scientists surgically removed part of the liver in a group of mice. `text(Ten days)` later, the scientists observed a low rate of DNA synthesis in the remaining liver cells.
Based on the information in Part `2`, which explanation is `ultext(best)` supported by this observation?

A.Choice: The liver is actively regenerating, and chromosomes are replicated as the cells prepare to divide.

B.Choice: Liver regeneration is switching from Mechanism `text(K)` to Mechanism `text(J)`, which does not require DNA synthesis.

C.Choice: The liver is increasing the rate of regeneration because more genes are expressed for specialized cell functions before cell division.

D.Choice: Liver regeneration is slowing or is complete because few liver cells are actively preparing for cell division by replicating DNA.

problems/TN25HSB/media/16a.jpg
Which statement `ultext(best)` explains the color variations in the population of peppered moths?

A.Choice: The air pollution prevented gas exchange in the light-colored moths, resulting in low survival rates.

B.Choice: The light-colored moths had better mechanisms for flight and migrated to a less-polluted environment.

Content: A research group collected data on populations of coral, shellfish, and sea grass in a small geographic area of the Pacific Ocean that experienced changes in ocean acidity level. The acidity of the ocean increases as the pH decreases. The data are shown in the table.
problems/TN25HSB/media/17a.jpg
Based on the data, which `ultext(three)` changes will `ultext(most likely)` occur if the pH continues to decrease in the study area?

A.Choice: The carrying capacity of animals that consume sea grass will decrease.

B.Choice: The carrying capacity of animals that consume sea grass will increase.

C.Choice: The populations of organisms that prey upon shellfish will increase as the population of shellfish decreases because of acidity.

D.Choice: The populations of herbivores that are better adapted to more acidic waters will increase.

E.Choice: The populations of organisms living on and around coral will decrease because of a decline in resources and habitat.

Content: Mutations in the gene encoding an enzyme can change the way an enzyme interacts with a substrate. The figure shows the enzyme-substrate interactions between a normal enzyme and an enzyme after mutation.
problems/TN25HSB/media/18a.jpg
How is the difference in the enzyme-substrate interaction because of the mutation `ultext(best)` explained?

A.Choice: The mutation changed the amino acid sequence of the protein, which resulted in a structural change in the active site.

B.Choice: The mutation changed the active site on the substrate, preventing collisions between the enzyme and the substrate.

C.Choice: The mutation created a new type of enzyme with a different active site that does not recognize the substrate.

D.Choice: The mutation affected the speed of the enzyme colliding with the substrate which affected the shape of the enzyme.
